Cell Theory.concept: Omnis cellula-e-cellula (All new cells arise from pre-existing cells) - stated by Rudolf Virchow.
Cell Theory.hint: Viruses are exceptions to the Cell Theory as they lack cellular machinery.

Mitochondria.concept: Site of aerobic respiration generating ATP. It has its own circular DNA and 70S ribosomes.
Mitochondria.hint: It is a semi-autonomous organelle. Found in large numbers in active cells like muscle cells.

Lysosomes.concept: Contains hydrolytic enzymes (acid hydrolases) active at acidic pH (~5.0) for intracellular digestion.
Lysosomes.hint: Highly abundant in macrophages and WBCs for destroying pathogens.

Ribosomes.trick: No Membrane = Universal Organelle (found in both Prokaryotes and Eukaryotes).
Ribosomes.concept: Known as the Protein Factory of the cell. Made of rRNA and proteins.
Ribosomes.hint: Prokaryotes have 70S (50S+30S), while Eukaryotes have 80S (60S+40S) ribosomes.

Endoplasmic Reticulum.trick: RER has dots (Ribosomes) = Proteins. SER is smooth = Lipids.
Endoplasmic Reticulum.concept: Intracellular transport system. SER detoxifies drugs in the liver.
Endoplasmic Reticulum.hint: Muscle cells have specialized SER called Sarcoplasmic Reticulum that stores Calcium.

Golgi Apparatus.trick: The Post Office of the Cell (Packages and Ships).
Golgi Apparatus.concept: Modifies, sorts, and packages proteins for secretion. Forms glycoproteins and glycolipids.
Golgi Apparatus.hint: Cis-face is the receiving end, Trans-face is the shipping end.

Nucleus.trick: Brain/Director of the cell. Discovered by Robert Brown.
Nucleus.concept: Contains genetic material (Chromatin) and Nucleolus (site for active rRNA synthesis).
Nucleus.hint: Mammalian mature RBCs lack a nucleus to accommodate more hemoglobin.

Plasma Membrane.trick: Fluid Mosaic Model = Icebergs of proteins floating in a sea of lipids.
Plasma Membrane.concept: Selectively permeable membrane primarily composed of a phospholipid bilayer and proteins.
Plasma Membrane.hint: Proposed by Singer and Nicolson in 1972.

Mitosis.concept: Equational division where one somatic cell divides into two identical diploid daughter cells.
Mitosis.hint: Best stage to study chromosome morphology (shape) is Metaphase.

Meiosis.trick: Meiosis I is Reductional (Chromosome number halves), Meiosis II is Equational.
Meiosis.concept: Occurs in germ cells to produce haploid gametes. Crossing over occurs in Pachytene stage.
Meiosis.hint: Chiasmata formation is the physical evidence of genetic recombination.

DNA Structure.trick: A double bonds with T (A=T), C triple bonds with G (C≡G).
DNA Structure.concept: Right-handed double helix. Backbone is made of sugar and phosphate.
DNA Structure.hint: The two strands are anti-parallel (5' to 3' and 3' to 5').

RNA Types.concept: rRNA is the most abundant. tRNA has a clover-leaf structure and carries amino acids.
RNA Types.hint: RNA contains Uracil instead of Thymine.

Transcription.trick: DNA to RNA = Transcribing the message.
Transcription.concept: RNA Polymerase binds to the Promoter and synthesizes mRNA in the 5' to 3' direction.
Transcription.hint: In eukaryotes, non-coding Introns are removed through Splicing.

Translation.trick: RNA to Protein = Translating the language of nucleotides into amino acids.
Translation.concept: Occurs in the cytoplasm on ribosomes. AUG is the universal start codon.
Translation.hint: UAA, UAG, and UGA are stop codons that terminate the process.

Central Dogma.concept: Unidirectional flow of genetic information proposed by Francis Crick.
Central Dogma.hint: Retroviruses (like HIV) show Reverse Central Dogma using Reverse Transcriptase.

Mendel First Law.trick: Law of Dominance = The stronger trait hides the weaker one.
Mendel First Law.concept: In a heterozygous condition, only the dominant allele expresses itself.
Mendel First Law.hint: Incomplete dominance (e.g., Snapdragon flowers) is an exception to this law.

Mendel Second Law.trick: Law of Segregation = Purity of Gametes.
Mendel Second Law.concept: Alleles separate during gamete formation so each gamete receives only one allele.
Mendel Second Law.hint: This law has NO exceptions in diploid organisms.

Blood Groups.trick: AB is the Universal Acceptor (No antibodies), O is the Universal Donor (No antigens).
Blood Groups.concept: Determined by multiple alleles (IA, IB, i). IA and IB show Co-dominance.
Blood Groups.hint: Rh factor determines positive or negative blood type. Erythroblastosis fetalis occurs in Rh- mother and Rh+ fetus.

Sex Determination.trick: Humans: XX (Female) / XY (Male). Birds: ZW (Female) / ZZ (Male).
Sex Determination.concept: In humans, the male heterogamety determines the sex of the child via the Y chromosome.
Sex Determination.hint: The SRY gene on the Y chromosome triggers male development.

Mutation.trick: Sudden heritable change. Coined by Hugo de Vries.
Mutation.concept: Point mutation involves a single base pair change (e.g., Sickle Cell Anemia).
Mutation.hint: Frameshift mutations are more dangerous as they alter the entire reading frame.

Evolution by Darwin.trick: Survival of the Fittest via Natural Selection.
Evolution by Darwin.concept: Nature selects variations that are most useful for survival in a given environment.
Evolution by Darwin.hint: Darwin's finches on the Galapagos Islands are a classic example of adaptive radiation.

Lamarckism.trick: Use and Disuse of Organs + Inheritance of Acquired Characters.
Lamarckism.concept: Proposed that traits acquired during a lifetime are passed to offspring (e.g., long neck of giraffe).
Lamarckism.hint: August Weismann disproved this with his Germplasm theory (cutting mice tails).

Human Heart.trick: Right side handles deoxygenated (blue), Left side handles oxygenated (red) blood.
Human Heart.concept: Four-chambered myogenic heart. SA Node is the natural pacemaker.
Human Heart.hint: Coronary arteries supply oxygenated blood directly to the heart muscles.

Double Circulation.trick: Systemic (Heart to Body) + Pulmonary (Heart to Lungs).
Double Circulation.concept: Ensures strict separation of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood in mammals and birds.
Double Circulation.hint: Amphibians and reptiles have incomplete double circulation (3-chambered heart).

Red Blood Cells.concept: Biconcave shape increases surface area. Destroyed in the Spleen (Graveyard of RBCs).
Red Blood Cells.hint: Formation of RBCs is called Erythropoiesis, stimulated by hormone erythropoietin from kidneys.

White Blood Cells.trick: Leukocytes = The Defense Army. Neutrophils are the most abundant.
White Blood Cells.concept: Protect against infections. Lymphocytes (B and T cells) provide specific immunity.
White Blood Cells.hint: Abnormal increase in WBC count is an indicator of Leukemia (Blood Cancer).

Platelets.concept: Cell fragments formed from Megakaryocytes in the bone marrow. Prevent excessive bleeding.
Platelets.hint: Dengue fever causes a massive drop in platelet count (Thrombocytopenia).

Nephron.trick: The structural and functional filtering unit of the kidney.
Nephron.concept: Consists of Bowman's capsule, Glomerulus, PCT, Henle's Loop, and DCT.
Nephron.hint: Glomerular filtration is a passive, non-selective process driven by blood pressure.

Urine Formation.concept: Maximum reabsorption of water and nutrients occurs in the PCT (Proximal Convoluted Tubule).
Urine Formation.hint: ADH (Vasopressin) makes the DCT and collecting duct permeable to water, concentrating the urine.

Neurons.concept: Longest cells in the body. They do not divide as they lack centrioles.
Neurons.hint: Myelin sheath acts as an insulator and speeds up nerve impulse conduction (Saltatory conduction).

Cerebrum.concept: Largest part of the brain. Responsible for memory, intelligence, speech, and voluntary movements.
Cerebrum.hint: Divided into two hemispheres connected by the Corpus Callosum.

Cerebellum.concept: Maintains posture, equilibrium, and coordinates smooth voluntary muscle movements.
Cerebellum.hint: Alcohol consumption primarily affects the cerebellum, causing staggering gait.

Pituitary Gland.concept: Located in the Sella turcica of the sphenoid bone. Controlled by the Hypothalamus.
Pituitary Gland.hint: Anterior lobe secretes Growth Hormone, while the Posterior lobe stores Oxytocin and ADH.

Thyroid Gland.concept: Secretes Thyroxine (T4) and Triiodothyronine (T3). Requires Iodine for hormone synthesis.
Thyroid Gland.hint: Deficiency of iodine causes Goiter. In children, it causes Cretinism (mental retardation).

Adrenal Gland.concept: Located above kidneys. Medulla secretes Adrenaline (Epinephrine) during emergencies.
Adrenal Gland.hint: Cortex secretes Cortisol (Life-saving/Stress hormone) and Aldosterone.

Pancreas Endocrine.trick: Islets of Langerhans: Alpha makes Glucagon, Beta makes Insulin.
Pancreas Endocrine.concept: Insulin lowers blood glucose, Glucagon raises it. They act antagonistically.
Pancreas Endocrine.hint: Lack of insulin leads to Diabetes Mellitus (high blood sugar).

Male Reproductive System.trick: Testes are outside the body for a reason.
Male Reproductive System.concept: Located in the scrotum to maintain a temperature 2-2.5°C lower than body temp for spermatogenesis.
Male Reproductive System.hint: Leydig cells secrete Testosterone, while Sertoli cells provide nutrition to sperm.

Female Reproductive System.concept: The endometrium of the uterus thickens and sheds cyclically (menstruation).
Female Reproductive System.hint: The Ampulla of the fallopian tube is the exact site of fertilization.

Menstrual Cycle.trick: Ovulation happens on the 14th day due to the LH Surge.
Menstrual Cycle.concept: Corpus luteum forms after ovulation and secretes Progesterone to maintain pregnancy.
Menstrual Cycle.hint: If fertilization does not occur, the corpus luteum degenerates into corpus albicans.

Fertilization.concept: Fusion of haploid male and female gametes to form a diploid zygote.
Fertilization.hint: Acrosome of the sperm releases enzymes (hyaluronidase) to penetrate the egg coverings.

Plasmodium Life Cycle.concept: Causes Malaria. Sporozoites are the infective stage injected by female Anopheles.
Plasmodium Life Cycle.hint: Hemozoin is the toxic substance released from ruptured RBCs causing chills and fever.

Antibodies.trick: GAMED = IgG, IgA, IgM, IgE, IgD.
Antibodies.concept: IgG can cross the placenta. IgA is found in colostrum (mother's milk) and saliva.
Antibodies.hint: IgE is primarily involved in allergic reactions.

Immunity Types.trick: Innate is by birth, Acquired is developed.
Immunity Types.concept: Active immunity: Body makes its own antibodies (slow but long-lasting). Passive: Readymade antibodies are given (fast but short-lived).
Immunity Types.hint: Vaccination is an example of artificial active immunity.

AIDS.concept: The virus specifically attacks and destroys Helper T-cells (CD4+ cells), paralyzing the immune system.
AIDS.hint: ELISA is the screening test, Western Blot is the confirmatory test.

Cancer.trick: Uncontrolled cell division. Tumors can be Benign or Malignant.
Cancer.concept: Malignant tumors show Metastasis (spreading to other parts of the body).
Cancer.hint: Cancer-causing genes are called Oncogenes. Normal cells have Proto-oncogenes.

Taxonomy.trick: Keep Pots Clean Or Family Gets Sick (Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species).
Taxonomy.concept: The hierarchical classification of life. Species is the basic and lowest unit of classification.
Taxonomy.hint: Carolus Linnaeus is the Father of Taxonomy.

Phylum Porifera.trick: Sponges = Pores all over the body.
Phylum Porifera.concept: Cellular level of organization. Possess a unique water canal system for food and oxygen gathering.
Phylum Porifera.hint: Choanocytes (collar cells) line the spongocoel and canals.

Phylum Arthropoda.concept: Largest phylum of Animalia. They have a chitinous exoskeleton and open circulatory system.
Phylum Arthropoda.hint: Respiration occurs through gills, book gills, book lungs, or tracheal system.

Phylum Chordata.trick: Four key features at some stage: Notochord, Nerve cord, Pharyngeal slits, Post-anal tail.
Phylum Chordata.concept: Includes vertebrates. The notochord is replaced by a vertebral column in adult vertebrates.
Phylum Chordata.hint: All vertebrates are chordates, but not all chordates are vertebrates.

Ozone Depletion.trick: Good ozone is UP (Stratosphere), Bad ozone is DOWN (Troposphere).
Ozone Depletion.concept: CFCs release active chlorine atoms that degrade ozone molecules into molecular oxygen.
Ozone Depletion.hint: Ozone thickness is measured in Dobson Units (DU).
